messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: Abline in Boxplot to short
parts:
Hello,

I try to put a reference line a 0 on my 'horizontal' boxplot.
But I have the problem that the line is to short. I think it
is related with the flipping of the axis. I can reproduce
the problem with a short example in 0.8.9 and in the dev version
0.9.0 (some weeks old):

GROUP <- factor(c(rep("a",100),rep("b",100),rep("c",100),rep("d",100),rep("e",100),rep("f",100)))
VAL <- c(rep(rnorm(100,0,0.5),6))
df <- data.frame(GROUP,VAL)

boxplot.test <- ggplot(df)+
geom_boxplot(aes(y=VAL,x=GROUP))+
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 0, linetype = 2)+
coord_flip()

I am doing something wrong or is there a problem with ggplot?
Maybe it is already fixed in the newest dev-version but I can't
remember how to update it?

best regards,
Johannes

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Abline in Boxplot to short
parts:
I took a look at this bug and I think I have it fixed... If you're interested in trying it out, it's in my experimental branch on GitHub.

You can install it with these commands:
install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
dev_mode()
install_github("ggplot2", "wch", "experimental")

See here for more information on using branches from github:
https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Using-ggplot2-branches


Here's some info on the bug in the issue tracker:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/361
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/364


Johannes - the "develop" branch you installed is outdated, which may be why you had problems. The branch where the development is happening is "master". The command that Brandon gave, install_github("ggplot2"), installs master by default.

-Winston
